points: Q3 2026 will show whether the 10% year-over-year Nights and Seats Booked growth reported in Q2 accelerated further through the summer travel peak or began to normalize.
The print will reveal if Gross Booking Value can stay at or above the Q2 16% year-over-year pace as ADR comps toughen and expansion-market growth mixes in.
It will test whether Adjusted EBITDA margin can hold near the 35% level while Airbnb Services expands into groceries, car rentals and airport pickups.

Management’s Q4 guide and any updated full-year 2026 commentary will show whether the post-Q2 outlook raise, which press reports suggest happened, is already captured in the 31.3% FY1 EPS growth consensus or leaves room for more.
MAR’s print three days earlier will provide a cross-check on leisure demand, pricing and occupancy trends heading into ABNB’s report.
The year-end setup depends on free cash flow margin staying around 35% and TTM FCF staying near $4.8B, backing the valuation case while the PEG sits at roughly sector median.
watch: Nights and Seats Booked y/y growth at or above 10% — supports the long.
GBV y/y growth at or above 16% — supports the long.
Adjusted EBITDA margin at or above 35% — supports the long.
Upward EPS revisions continuing to outpace downgrades, in line with the recent 24/5 ratio — supports the long.
